content:
I'm wondering what the plan is with LocallyIntegrable vs LocallyIntegrableOn, and if we might not want to just nuke LocallyIntegrable.

Maybe it is just confirmation bias, but I keep running into situations where I have LocallyIntegrable in the goal, but some lemma I want is available only for LocallyIntegrableOn. Of course this is easily fixed, but I'm wondering if the philosophy here is that this should be considered missing API for LocallyIntegrable (though that leads to a bit of duplication?), or if we're just supposed to perform the obvious fix in place, but in that case it seems we should just do without LocallyIntegrable.

Triggered by PR #41733 (I needed the first one specifically). Tagging @Floris van Doorn since you are the original author.

You could redefine LocallyIntegrable to be an abbrev for LocallyIntegrableOn univ and then the API will probably just work.

Or you could just make all the API :-) It would be easy, using docs#MeasureTheory.locallyIntegrableOn_univ
Indeed it is easy, the theorems in my PR are all one line passing through that. The question is rather "Is this a good idea?"
I guess the abbrev might be a good hybrid approach, but it feels a bit sketchy
Duplicate it is then. I'll just PR when it comes up.
